quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Supply chain managers direct or coordinate production, purchasing, warehousing, distribution or financial forecasting, look for ways to streamline activities, and direct the movement, storage or processing of inventory.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Supply Chain Managers) include Supply Chain Manager, Supply Chain Director, Global Supply Chain Director and Material Requirements Planning Manager.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a supply chain manager does
paragraphs: Supply chain managers direct or coordinate production, purchasing, warehousing, distribution or financial forecasting, look for ways to streamline activities, and direct the movement, storage or processing of inventory.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Supply Chain Managers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Manage purchasing, material requirements planning and inventory control.
Define the measures used to compare and evaluate supply chain performance.
Put new or improved supply chain processes in place.
Coordinate supply chain management with other functions such as sales and marketing.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: Supply Chain Analyst; Procurement Manager; Logistics Manager.
Less common routes on the map: MBA (Master of Business Administration).
